title: Bearings
summary: Learn how to read, draw and reverse compass bearings using North, clockwise angles and three-figure notation.

items.prompt: From P, the clockwise angle from North to Q is $47^\circ$. What is the bearing of Q from P?
items.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from North and written using three figures, so $47^\circ$ is written as $047^\circ$.

items.prompt: At C, D is $35^\circ$ anticlockwise from North. What is the bearing of D from C?
items.explanation: A bearing is measured clockwise from North. The clockwise angle is $360^\circ-35^\circ=325^\circ$.

items.prompt: Point Q is due south-east of P. Which of these could be the bearing of Q from P?
items.explanation: South-east is halfway between east ($090^\circ$) and south ($180^\circ$), giving a bearing of $135^\circ$.

items.prompt: The bearing of B from A is $068^\circ$. What is the bearing of A from B?
items.explanation: Reverse bearings differ by $180^\circ$. Since $68+180=248$, the bearing of A from B is $248^\circ$.

items.prompt: A boat sails from H on a bearing of $210^\circ$. In which general direction does it travel?
items.explanation: The bearing $210^\circ$ lies between south ($180^\circ$) and west ($270^\circ$), so the boat travels down and to the left.
